topic: Rank-normalization phase transition for honest Synthetic Survival Control bands. In the right-censored exact-factor panel model, canonically write S^0_{p,m}(t)=s_p(t)+b_p(t)'z_m and define W_r^* as the minimax expected sup-width among uniformly honest continuous-time bands for the target post-control survival curve. Prove the sharp frontier W_1^* asymptotic to (N0 KD)^(-1/2), because normalization makes target-pre data ancillary at exact rank one, versus W_r^* asymptotic to KT^(-1/2)+(N0 KD)^(-1/2) for every fixed r>=2 under explicit survival, censor-overlap, smoothness and contrast-Gram bounds, uniformly over all sufficiently large N0, KT and KD without relative-growth restrictions. Construct an attaining censoring-aware functional-PCR martingale-multiplier band with controlled grid interpolation and matching normalization-preserving Le Cam lower bounds for both channels. Replace the PETAL Synthetic Survival Control donor bootstrap by the resulting honest patient-level band. Do not retreat to pointwise inference, balanced-only asymptotics, rank>=2 alone, or a bootstrap-validity theorem without the matching minimax converse.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine the sharp rank-normalization phase transition in the minimax expected sup-width of uniformly honest continuous-time bands for a post-control Synthetic Survival Control curve: donor-patient noise only at exact rank one, versus an additional target-pre factor-loading channel at every fixed rank at least two.

source_refs.claim: SSC uses Kaplan-Meier curves followed by rank-r PCR and proves a finite-grid consistency rate; its PETAL analysis reports a 500-donor-bootstrap 95% interval, not an honest continuous-time band or minimax converse.
source_refs.author: Jessy Xinyi Han and Devavrat Shah

source_refs.claim: Synthetic-control prediction uncertainty has distinct pre-treatment weight-estimation and post-treatment stochastic-error components, but the paper treats scalar panel outcomes rather than censored survival processes or rank-normalization degeneracy.
source_refs.author: Matias D. Cattaneo, Yingjie Feng, and Rocio Titiunik
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: Factor-model synthetic-control inference depends on whether time- or unit-level confounding supplies the relevant randomness, establishing a nearby two-channel phenomenon but not the survival-curve rank-one normalization frontier.
source_refs.author: Guido W. Imbens and Davide Viviano

source_refs.excerpt: Sampling error and estimated quantile error are outside this proposal.
the converse uses the literal equal-count subfamily with k_n=ceil(m_n), whose rate is equivalent up to constants
Combining the two lower bounds ... proves

open_problems.why_unsolved: Han-Shah stop at a finite-grid consistency bound and empirical donor bootstrap; they do not propagate patient-level Kaplan-Meier martingales through estimated PCR singular spaces or study expected band width. Scalar synthetic-control inference separates pre-weight and post-prediction uncertainty, but does not exploit the survival normalization S(0)=1, whose rank-one geometry may make target-pre data ancillary. The prior distributional-SC proposal explicitly excluded sampling and estimated-curve error, while the functional-DiD lineage supplies separate upper and lower subexperiments only for a different causal curve. The missing proof is therefore a rank-specific derivative and information calculation: compose censoring martingales with PCR, prove the target-pre derivative vanishes at rank one but not rank at least two, and construct normalization-preserving Le Cam pairs isolating every surviving channel without imposing relative growth.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Uniform-honesty upper and Le Cam lower-bound theorems showing W_1^* has order (N0 KD)^(-1/2) and W_r^* has order KT^(-1/2)+(N0 KD)^(-1/2) for each fixed r>=2 without relative-growth restrictions, together with a continuous-time censoring-aware PCR martingale-multiplier band attaining those widths.

writing_exemplar.why: Mirror its application-led arc from censored, sparse time-to-event panels to a low-rank survival counterfactual, then make its empirical bootstrap the precise inferential deficiency to resolve.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Clinical when-if questions require an entire counterfactual survival trajectory -> SSC supplies low-rank identification and PCR consistency under censoring -> PETAL uncertainty is currently a donor-bootstrap robustness display -> honest patient-level bands require the rank-dependent information channels and their minimax widths

method_exemplars.technique: Use the fixed-design error-in-variables PCR minimum-norm identification and row-space/out-of-sample span argument, then differentiate that map under the canonical survival normalization.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Han-Shah import this PCR stability machinery; the desired theorem must refine its prediction map enough to expose the rank-one zero derivative and the rank-at-least-two target-pre direction.

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over the counting-process martingale representation and wild/multiplier resampling proof for time-simultaneous survival bands, jointly resampling donor and target patient martingales.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the uniform-in-time Gaussian and multiplier step absent from SSC; the new work is to compose it with estimated PCR weights and retain both uncertainty channels.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the decomposition of in-sample weight uncertainty and out-of-sample prediction uncertainty, including separate probability control for each component.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested width is a sum of two source-specific contributions for r>=2; survival normalization supplies the new degeneracy removing one contribution at r=1.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize whether a single uniformly honest Synthetic Survival Control band can adapt to unknown rank and attain the rank-one donor-only width while retaining coverage over rank-two alternatives, and if not, give the sharp singular-value separation required for such adaptation.

source_refs.claim: SSC chooses the PCR rank by a gap rule, elbow, or cross-validation, but its theorem conditions on the selected rank and does not establish post-selection coverage.
source_refs.author: Jessy Xinyi Han and Devavrat Shah

source_refs.claim: Honest rank-adaptive matrix-completion confidence sets are governed by composite testing rates and can fail in some noise regimes, but are studied in Frobenius rather than survival-functional geometry.
source_refs.author: Alexandra Carpentier, Olga Klopp, Matthias Loffler, and Richard Nickl

open_problems.why_unsolved: The target width changes discontinuously between exact ranks one and two, while Han-Shah's data-driven rank choice has no inferential guarantee. Existing honest rank-adaptation theory reduces adaptation to composite testing in matrix-completion geometry, not normalized monotone survival curves with censoring and a post-control sup-functional. A small second factor can be contiguous to rank one yet activate the KT^(-1/2) target-pre channel. The missing obstacle is thus a testing boundary for normalization-preserving rank-two perturbations, not merely consistency of a tuning rule.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An adaptive-honesty or impossibility theorem over the union of rank-one and rank-two survival-factor classes, with a sharp second-singular-value separation boundary and an attaining rank-test-plus-band procedure on the separated classes.

writing_exemplar.why: Mirror its formulation of honest adaptation as a composite hypothesis-testing question rather than treating rank selection as a tuning detail.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Low-rank structure yields faster inference on smaller submodels -> honesty requires distinguishing the smaller rank class from nearby higher-rank alternatives -> testing geometry determines whether adaptation is possible -> normalized censored survival panels need a rank-one versus rank-two separation frontier

method_exemplars.technique: Port the reduction from adaptive confidence sets to low-rank composite testing and the test-plus-oracle-confidence-set construction.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The resolution is exactly an honest adaptation problem, but with sup-width for a causal curve and normalization-preserving survival alternatives.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt debiasing and sharp distributional characterization of low-rank factors and entries to construct the rank-test statistic and conditional band after selection.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It provides low-rank uncertainty quantification at the factor-estimation layer that rank-adaptive SSC must combine with censored functional noise.

method_exemplars.technique: Use multiplier-resampled martingale processes to calibrate the survival-function sup statistic after rank testing.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The ultimate adaptive set is a time-simultaneous survival band, not a Frobenius ball.

open_problems.open_problem: Develop sharp honest sup-norm bands for Synthetic Survival Control under quantitatively approximate rather than exact low rank, with band width separating approximation bias from target-pre and donor-patient stochastic channels.

source_refs.claim: Han-Shah motivate low rank through Taylor approximation of smooth nonlinear survival models, but their theory assumes an exact finite-rank factorization, well-conditioned spectrum, and exact post-factor span.
source_refs.author: Jessy Xinyi Han and Devavrat Shah

source_refs.claim: Linear synthetic controls can be biased for expected survival time and survival curves under standard nonlinear survival data-generating processes, even after alternative-scale transformations.
source_refs.author: Alicia Curth, Hoifung Poon, Aditya V. Nori, and Javier Gonzalez
source_refs.venue: Proceedings of Machine Learning Research, Causal Learning and Reasoning

source_refs.claim: Nuclear-norm matrix completion estimates causal panel counterfactuals under low complexity and structured missingness, but does not provide honest continuous-time censored-survival bands or a bias-aware minimax width.
source_refs.author: Susan Athey, Mohsen Bayati, Nikolay Doudchenko, Guido W. Imbens, and Khashayar Khosravi
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

open_problems.why_unsolved: There is a direct tension between Han-Shah's approximate-model motivation and exact-rank proof class, sharpened by Curth et al.'s demonstration that nonlinear survival distributions can make linear synthetic survival summaries biased. Low-rank panel and matrix-completion theory controls prediction error but does not translate a functional singular-value tail or post-span defect into honest sup-band bias. The first proof step that changes is deterministic: exact row-space inclusion must become an oracle inequality for the post-factor projection residual; multiplier calibration then needs an estimable or sensitivity-indexed bias envelope, and the converse must vary both the tail factor and the two sampling channels.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A minimax theorem over a named approximate-factor class, such as bounded functional singular-value tail plus post-span defect, giving an honest band whose width equals a sharp approximation-bias modulus plus the applicable target-pre and donor-patient rates, with a matching lower bound.

writing_exemplar.why: Use its distinction between matching a synthetic object and recovering a scientifically meaningful survival distribution to motivate an explicit misspecification radius.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Synthetic controls rely on linear reconstruction -> survival data-generating processes and distributional summaries can violate that linearity -> exact low rank can hide structural bias -> honest SSC inference must price a quantified approximate-factor residual into the band

method_exemplars.technique: Replace its exact out-of-sample row-space condition by a quantitative projection-residual version and propagate the residual through minimum-norm PCR prediction.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The resolution requires a characterization of exactly how failure of post-factor span biases the SSC curve.

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over nuclear-norm low-complexity regularization and structured panel prediction bounds as an oracle estimator for an approximate-rank survival surface.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Approximate rank is naturally encoded by low-complexity tails rather than a hard PCR cutoff; the new theorem must convert prediction bias into uniform causal-curve coverage.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt their principled enlargement for misspecified synthetic-control prediction to a functional bias modulus combined with censored martingale quantiles.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the closest inferential template explicitly separating weight-estimation uncertainty from out-of-sample misspecification.

open_problems.open_problem: When may deterministic smoothing, PCR-truncation, and grid-interpolation bias inflation be omitted from a censoring-aware Synthetic Survival Control multiplier band, and can failure be certified by a matching normalization-preserving undercoverage witness?

source_refs.excerpt: the necessity frontier for an uninflated multiplier band remains open.
The honest band is bias-aware for known s and L

open_problems.why_unsolved: Gaussian or multiplier coupling calibrates the stochastic supremum but does not absorb a first-order deterministic shift. The prior functional-DiD proposal leaves necessity of inflation open; censored SSC additionally introduces Kaplan-Meier drift, estimated PCR eigenspaces, and time-grid interpolation constrained by survival normalization. The first changed proof step is shifted-process comparison: the standardized aggregate bias must be controlled before anti-concentration can transfer multiplier critical values, while necessity requires a model-valid local sequence whose shift survives normalization and produces nonvanishing undercoverage.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An if-and-only-if shifted-Gaussian coverage criterion for an uninflated SSC band, plus a feasible diagnostic and a censored factor-panel sequence proving nonvanishing undercoverage whenever the criterion fails.

writing_exemplar.why: Its progression from a functional causal target to multiplier bands provides the nearest framing for why simultaneous curve inference needs more than a point estimator.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Curve-valued causal target -> multiplier calibration for simultaneous inference -> reconstruction or projection leaves a deterministic shift -> characterize exactly when an uninflated band remains honest

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over shifted-hyperrectangle Gaussian comparison, multiplier covariance control, and anti-concentration to a growing survival-time grid.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired criterion is an exact coverage comparison for a supremum after a nonnegligible deterministic displacement.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt worst-case bias accounting and honest critical-value logic to the functional-PCR survival curve.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the explicit bias-versus-variance logic needed to decide when deterministic inflation is unavoidable.

open_problems.open_problem: Construct uniformly honest continuous-time Synthetic Survival Control bands under covariate-dependent censoring using estimated inverse-probability-of-censoring weights, and determine the extra width or efficiency loss caused by censoring-nuisance estimation in each rank regime.

source_refs.claim: Han-Shah assume non-informative censoring, identify IPCW or joint modeling as a future extension, and leave time-to-event estimators other than Kaplan-Meier to future work.
source_refs.author: Jessy Xinyi Han and Devavrat Shah

source_refs.claim: IPCW Kaplan-Meier and Cox procedures use time-dependent prognostic factors to correct dependent censoring, but do not address latent-factor synthetic counterfactuals or continuous-time PCR bands.
source_refs.author: James M. Robins and Dianne M. Finkelstein

source_refs.claim: Empirical survival-control comparisons can be badly biased when longer times are systematically more likely to be censored, making censoring assumptions consequential rather than cosmetic.
source_refs.author: Alicia Curth, Hoifung Poon, Aditya V. Nori, and Javier Gonzalez
source_refs.venue: Proceedings of Machine Learning Research, Causal Learning and Reasoning

open_problems.why_unsolved: Han-Shah's proof begins with a uniform Kaplan-Meier error bound under independent censoring; estimated IPCW replaces it with a two-step time-indexed process whose nuisance error is correlated across time and amplified by PCR singular-space estimation. Existing IPCW identifies and estimates survival under dependent censoring but does not handle latent-factor synthetic counterfactuals. The first changed proof step is the donor-curve influence expansion: each Kaplan-Meier martingale becomes an IPCW influence function plus a censoring-score correction, after which orthogonality or cross-fitting is needed before functional PCR and multiplier calibration.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sufficient-condition theorem for an IPCW or orthogonalized functional-PCR estimator with a uniform Gaussian or multiplier limit and honest continuous-time band under explicit censor-overlap and nuisance-rate conditions, plus a minimax or semiparametric efficiency characterization of whether nuisance estimation adds a width term at rank one or rank at least two.

writing_exemplar.why: Its conclusion names dependent censoring and IPCW as an unresolved clinical limitation, so its motivation naturally lands on this destination.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: SSC handles sparse censored panels under non-informative censoring -> real clinical loss to follow-up can depend on prognosis -> the current Kaplan-Meier and PCR guarantee then loses validity -> an IPCW-orthogonalized honest band is needed for the same post-control survival target

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over inverse-probability-of-censoring weighted risk sets based on time-dependent prognostic histories and the accompanying observed-data identification argument.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It directly replaces the independent-censoring Kaplan-Meier first stage that Han-Shah identify as their limitation.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the two-step Kaplan-Meier functional CLT and bootstrap-validity arguments for censored causal treatment-effect functionals.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies uniform empirical-process theory for a causal estimand with right censoring and estimated first steps, structurally close to the IPCW SSC curve before PCR composition.

method_exemplars.technique: Use martingale wild-bootstrap constructions that jointly mimic baseline and regression-parameter estimation to calibrate a time-simultaneous band.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Estimated censoring weights and estimated PCR factors create the same need to preserve dependence among multiple process components in the multiplier law.

literature_map:
1. Han and Shah (2025, arXiv:2511.14133) are the direct anchor: low-rank causal survival panels, Kaplan-Meier first stages, finite-grid PCR consistency, and a 500-donor-bootstrap PETAL interval, but no uniform-honesty or minimax-width theorem.
2. Their theory conditions on exact rank, well-conditioned spectrum, and exact post-factor span, although the motivation uses approximate Taylor expansions of nonlinear survival models.
3. Curth, Poon, Nori, and Gonzalez (2024, CLeaR/PMLR; arXiv:2312.00501) show that ordinary synthetic controls can bias survival summaries because linear averaging changes distributional shape.
4. Curth et al. also document the danger of non-random censoring, while Han-Shah explicitly list IPCW or joint modeling as future work.
5. Cattaneo, Feng, and Titiunik (2021, JASA; arXiv:1912.07120) decompose scalar SC uncertainty into pre-weight and post-prediction components, the closest analogue of the proposed two-channel width.
6. Imbens and Viviano (2026 version, arXiv:2312.00955) show factor-model SC inference changes with time- versus unit-level confounding, but do not study normalized survival functions.
7. Agarwal, Shah, and Shen (2023, arXiv:2010.14449) provide the minimum-norm PCR identification, row-space condition, and out-of-sample stability machinery imported by SSC.
8. Athey, Bayati, Doudchenko, Imbens, and Khosravi (2021, JASA; arXiv:1710.10251) supply low-complexity matrix-completion counterfactuals, but not censored continuous-time inference.
9. Arkhangelsky, Athey, Hirshberg, Imbens, and Wager (2021, AER; arXiv:1812.09970) prove asymptotic normality for latent-factor synthetic DiD, again for scalar rather than survival-curve outcomes.
10. Goldsmith, Greven, and Crainiceanu (2013, Biometrics, DOI:10.1111/j.1541-0420.2012.01808.x) construct simultaneous FPC bands accounting for decomposition uncertainty, but without censoring or a causal post-control target.
11. Dobler, Pauly, and Scheike (2019, Biometrics; arXiv:1808.00242) provide the closest martingale-multiplier technology for time-simultaneous hazard and survival inference.
12. Sant'Anna (2016, arXiv:1604.02642) proves functional CLTs and bootstrap validity for two-step Kaplan-Meier causal treatment-effect processes, but not latent-factor panels.
13. Robins and Finkelstein (2000, Biometrics) provide IPCW correction for dependent censoring, not yet combined with functional-PCR synthetic controls.
14. Carpentier, Klopp, Loffler, and Nickl (2018, Bernoulli; arXiv:1608.04861) show honest rank adaptation is controlled by composite testing rates, making unknown-rank SSC bands a separate frontier.
15. Exact searches pairing synthetic survival control with confidence band, minimax, functional principal component, rank selection, and informative censoring found no paper occupying the normalized-rank continuous-time minimax-band problem.
